question: What is the reality of Salat al-Tasbih, and is it permissible to pray it?
asked: Is there something called Salat al-Tasbih? I've heard some controversy over this, so can you shed some light on it?
answer:
Salat al-Tasbih is a specific prayer that has been narrated in a hadith reported in a number of books, Abu Dawood and Tirmidhi and the Mustadrak of al-Hakim and other books of hadith, in which the Prophet ﷺ is reported to have said to his uncle al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib: "O my uncle, O Abbas, should I not gift you? Should I not give you something of benefit? Should I not do something that will help you? I will tell you ten things; if you do them, Allah shall forgive all of your sins: the first of them and the last of them, the ancient of them and the newest of them, the intentional of them and the unintentional of them, the large of them and the small of them, the secret of them and the hidden of them."

That you pray four raka'at, and in every single raka'ah you begin with the Fatiha and then a surah. And once you finish the surah, then before you go into the ruku', you say "Subhanallah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar" fifteen times. And then you go into ruku', and you say, after the tasbih, the same thing ten times. Then when you stand up, you say it also ten times. Then when you go into sajdah, you say it also ten times. Then when you sit between the two sajdahs, you say it ten times. Then when you go to the second sajdah, you say it ten times. And then when you stand up, before you begin the Fatiha, you say it ten times as well. And that will be 75 times. Then you repeat the cycle every single raka'ah; that will be 75 times for every single raka'ah. You do that for four raka'at.

And then the hadith allegedly says: if you are able to do this prayer once a day, then do so. If not, then at least every week do so. If not, then at least every month do so. If not, then at least once every year do so. And if not, then at least once in your lifetime do so.

Now, this hadith is a very interesting discussion, and many treatises have been written just about this hadith. It is fair to say that this hadith has been one of the most controversial (obviously there are many of this nature), one of the most hotly contested and debated with regards to its authenticity throughout Islamic history. And believe it or not, we have the entire spectrum. It is one of the few hadith that our scholars have differed over so much. Generally speaking, when scholars differ over a hadith, it's basically one shade between here or there: is it da'if or is it hasan? This hadith has proven to be so contentious, for reasons beyond the scope of our lecture.

But just for your information's sake, we have had scholars through the entire spectrum of this hadith. There are some that have even made this hadith sahih li-ghayrihi, which is basically one of the highest levels. And there are those like al-Suyuti who have said it is hasan, it is a good hadith. And there are those like Ali al-Madini and like Imam Ahmad and like Ibn Khuzaymah; they have said it is da'if. And there are those that have said it is da'if jiddan. And there are even those, Ibn al-Jawzi for example, who say it is a fabricated hadith. So we have from fabricated all the way to authentic, and all the shades in the middle.

The reasons are, again, beyond the scope of our Q&A here, because it deals with the technicalities of hadith sciences. Suffice to state that the issue is that this hadith does not have a single authentic chain; rather, it has a multitude of weak chains. So the question then comes to the scholar of hadith: when he looks at these weak chains, do they aid one another? Do they support one another to the level of acceptability, hasan? And then there is also a philosophy out there, which is a very minor philosophy, a very small group of scholars, who said that if there's a lot of da'if and hasan, they might even get to sahih li-ghayrihi. That is not the mainstream position, but it is out there. And so those scholars even said it has been boosted to that level.

You should know that most of the early scholars of hadith considered this narration to be not authentic, and that's something that is very important. Because generally speaking, one finds the giants of the field in hadith, Imam Ahmad and the early scholars, Ali al-Madini, who was the teacher of Imam al-Bukhari; these are the main, the big names, and we know for a fact that all of those early scholars considered this hadith to be not authentic.

Also, by the way, the hadith simply sounds strange, to be honest. Those who are experts in hadith, those who immerse their lives in hadith and collect and narrate hadith, simply reading this hadith, something seems off about it. They don't seem to be the wordings of our Prophet ﷺ, and something seems to be not correct about this.

Nonetheless, that is an opinion. There are opinions that consider this hadith to be authentic: al-Suyuti, and also a scholar in our times, Shaykh al-Albani, who is known to be somebody who spent an entire lifetime specializing in hadith sciences. He has contributed immensely; friend and foe alike acknowledge that Shaykh al-Albani has really done a lot of service to the Sunnah and the hadith books. And he has considered this hadith also to be authentic, along with many of his students. And so we have this healthy controversy in this regard.

Therefore, these are issues that we should not make something very clear-cut over. We should not say it is haram or wrong. Rather, you're asking me my opinion personally, and I say that I follow here what Imam Ahmad said. Imam Ibn Hanbal was asked about this hadith, as reported in the famous book al-Mughni of Ibn Qudama, the Hanbali madhhab book. Ibn Qudama said that as for Salat al-Tasbih, Imam Ahmad said, "I don't like to do it." So he was asked why not, and he moved his hands like this and said, "There is nothing authentic about it." There's nothing authentic narrated about it. And Imam Ahmad therefore considers the hadith to be weak, and so he does not consider this salah to be mustahab, or something that should be done.

And then Ibn Qudama, the famous scholar of the Hanbali madhhab (in fact, he is the giant of the Hanbali tradition; he has written a number of books, and al-Mughni is considered to be one of the primary references and encyclopedias of the madhhab), Ibn Qudama narrates that Imam Ahmad said, "I don't like it, and I'd rather not do it." Then he says: however, if a person prays it, there's no problem. When it comes to these supererogatory prayers, we do not condition that there be something authentic; we can act upon a weak hadith in this regard.

So Ibn Qudama makes a very good point. Even if the hadith is not authentic, so what? At the end of the day, it is a salah. You are standing facing the qibla, with wudu; you are bowing your head to Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. At the end of the day, all of these that you are saying are adhkar: subhanAllah, alhamdulillah, la ilaha illallah, Allahu akbar. At the end of the day, it's four raka'at nafl. So don't make such a major issue or controversy, and do not ever call this a bid'ah. In my opinion, this is a complete, blatant disregard of the reality of what a bid'ah is. It cannot be a bid'ah, because you are following what you think is a Sunnah. Even if it is a da'if hadith, it is allowed by many scholars; in fact, it is the majority opinion that you may practice a weak hadith as long as the general rubric of what you are doing is something that is allowed.

So while I personally do not pray Salat al-Tasbih, and I've never prayed Salat al-Tasbih as of yet, because I consider this hadith to be not authentic (I personally would not do that simply because I find the wordings to be something bizarre; it just doesn't seem to be something that the Prophet ﷺ said), nonetheless, as Ibn Qudama says, even if it is weak, if somebody chooses to opt for this and practice this hadith, at the end of the day, honestly, what's the big deal? It's four raka'at sunnah, meaning four raka'at, not a fard prayer. And you are doing everything legit, and you are saying adhkar within the salah, and you think that you are following either an authentic hadith, if you follow Shaykh al-Albani or some of the other scholars, al-Suyuti and others, or, even if you think like Imam Ahmad said that the hadith is da'if, you might be following the position that it is permissible to act upon a da'if hadith.

So therefore, **whoever chooses to do this, they have precedent and they have scholarship, and they have a basis and a legitimate paradigm, and no one should criticize that person.** And whoever says, "You know what, something seems a bit off about this, and I'd rather stick with what I'm more comfortable doing," well, that person has also done something good, and they have remained clear of an area or a matter that might be gray. And if they don't pray Salat al-Tasbih, make sure that they do something else.

Because, again, I conclude on this point before I move to the next question: all too often some of our brothers are very harsh or strict about an action of worship that they think is wrong (and maybe they're right; sometimes it might be wrong), and they don't provide a substitute. And so what happens is, an innocent Muslim might have wanted to pray some prayer that he thinks is good, like this one, and some brother comes: "Oh, this is haram," or "This is bid'ah," or "This is wrong," and then no substitute is provided. So you end up basically not helping the spirituality of this person; you end up just coming and destroying something good that they wanted to do.

So my humble suggestion is that if you feel that this salah is not something that should be performed, okay, no problem: pray Salat al-Duha, pray extra nafl at any time, pray tahajjud once in a while. So my point is: make sure you are not amongst those people who all they do is destroy and refute and make things harsh, and they don't provide a substitute. Be careful that we have that healthy balance. I personally do not pray Salat al-Tasbih, but try to pray other salawat regularly as well, that inshallah can have that portion of your life. Because really, it is important that we understand that there is a need to be spiritual; there is a need to do these rituals. And when you shut off doors, make sure that you allow other doors as well.

So in the end, Allah knows best. I personally don't do it; however, whoever wants to do it, there is precedent in doing that. And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best.
